title: Beyond Looking Up, Try Looking Around: Harmonizing Global Structure and Local Consistency in Optimal Transport for Short Text Clustering
claim: Methods that assign labels using only sample-to-label cost misassign similar neighbors; adding sample-to-sample consistency corrects these errors.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, central 'Correcting' transition arrows under a 'Semantic consistency' banner
description: A three-panel schematic reading left to right. The left panel, titled (a) Existing OT, shows blue triangles and green squares as samples. Dashed lines connect each sample to a blue or green hexagon, which is its pseudo-label. A curved dark dashed decision boundary cuts through the clusters. Red rounded boxes mark misidentified samples that sit on the wrong side of the boundary. Curved gradient arrows labelled 'Correcting' lead to a middle panel. There, circles group the neighboring samples of each class, and links between samples are drawn inside each circle. A black gradient arrow reading 'Semantic consistency' spans the top and points to the right panel, (b) CAOT. That panel shows clean clusters separated by a straight dashed boundary, with every sample connected to the right hexagon. A legend at the bottom explains samples, pseudo-labels, decision boundary and misidentified samples. The eye goes first to the red boxes and the large blue and green hexagons.
caption: {\fontsize{8.89}{9}\selectfont Schematic illustration of the motivation. Existing methods rely solely on the transport cost from samples to candidate pseudo-labels (hexagons), where the cost is visualized as the distances from triangles to hexagons, causing semantically similar neighbors to be assigned different pseudo-labels (red boxes). The proposed CAOT addresses this issue by incorporating sample-to-sample semantic consistency, thereby correcting these misassignments. }
abstract: Pseudo-labeling based on Optimal Transport (OT) has become an effective mechanism for enhancing short text clustering. Existing OT methods are short in modeling semantic consistencies between samples, which may assign different pseudo-labels to semantically similar samples. These erroneous pseudo-labels can cause the model to produce inferior clusters. This paper proposes a novel short text clustering framework, which remedies the neglect of semantic consistency in existing OT methods, generating reliable pseudo-labels to facilitate clustering. Specifically, the proposed approach first designs an instance-level attention mechanism to capture semantic relationships between samples, which are then integrated into the OT formulation to endow the transport process with neighborhood semantic awareness. By solving the proposed OT formulation, reliable pseudo-labels are obtained that simultaneously account for sample-to-sample semantic consistency and sample-to-cluster global structure information. These pseudo-labels are then used as supervisory signals to guide the model to achieve accurate clustering. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at: \href{https://github.com/YZH0905/CAOT-STC}{https://github.com/YZH0905/CAOT-STC}.
